approved_by: study owner, FINAL_FREEZE_AND_START_B200.md §3 (2026-10-06): revision-2 rule (aligned evidence is not automatically mandatory) approved; eight needs-review decisions and 14 flagged-item repairs applied; approval recorded after contract/rules/audit consistency and leak checks

functional_semantics.triton: C[b] = A[b] @ B[b] via a (BATCH, M, K) view of A and a (BATCH, N, K) transposed copy of B; output flat (BATCH*M*N,) in A's dtype (impl_triton.py 133-136, 86-97).
functional_semantics.cutile: C[b] = A[b] @ B[b] via (BATCH, M, K) and (BATCH, K, N) views; output c_3d.reshape(-1) in A's dtype (impl_cutile.py 82-84, 52-72, 130).
functional_semantics.note: Both compute the reference torch.matmul(A_3d, B_3d).view(-1) (impl_torch.py 9-12); the result is the same, but the operand layout one side consumes differs (see preprocessing).

stages.triton: Output allocation (134), B^T lookup/materialisation (136, first call only), host descriptors (141/153), one GEMM kernel launch over (ceil(M/tm), ceil(N/tn), BATCH) (impl_triton.py 139-162).
stages.cutile: Output allocation (84), host grid/K-tile arithmetic (118-121), one GEMM kernel launch over (ceil(M/tm)*ceil(N/tn), BATCH) (impl_cutile.py 118-128), flat view return (130).
stages.note: The GEMM stage itself is identical (single launch, full-K per tile). The extra first-call transpose stage on one side is a boundary issue tracked under preprocessing/intermediate_storage.

dependencies.triton: Output tiles independent; sequential K loop inside a program (impl_triton.py 86-94).

reduction_scan_sort.triton: K reduced sequentially in chunks into one fp32 accumulator by tl.dot with accumulator operand; no split-K/atomics (impl_triton.py 84-94).
reduction_scan_sort.cutile: K reduced sequentially in chunks (compile-time trip count) into one fp32 accumulator by ct.mma; no split-K/atomics (impl_cutile.py 47-68).
reduction_scan_sort.note: Same reduction structure; grouped/swizzled tile raster on both sides is launch-order only.

precision.triton: fp32 accumulator (84); tl.dot(..., input_precision="tf32") (94); cast to output dtype (96).
precision.cutile: fp32 accumulator (47); operands cast to ct.tfloat32 for fp32 inputs, else native (50, 64-65); cast at store (72).
precision.note: Same precision class, matching the reference's allow_tf32 = True (impl_torch.py 4); config.yaml verify atol 1.0 / rtol 1e-2.

preprocessing.triton: _b_transposed (44-51) materialises B^T = B.view(BATCH, K, N).transpose(1, 2).contiguous() on the first call for a given B tensor object and memoises it in a WeakTensorKeyDictionary (41); run() calls it every time (136), so warmup and timed repeats consume a prepacked (BATCH, N, K) operand without paying the transpose.
preprocessing.cutile: A.contiguous().view / B.contiguous().view (82-83) are zero-copy for the contiguous generator tensors; B is consumed in its given (BATCH, K, N) layout by the kernel (58-62).
preprocessing.note: Decided 2026-10-06 (owner, FINAL_FREEZE_AND_START_B200.md §3): B is delivered row-major; consuming it directly (cuTile side) or through a repacked/transposed copy rebuilt by device work inside every run() is a mapping choice, so the layout divergence is mapping-only. Any cross-call input-identity / data-pointer / value cache of a transformed operand is forbidden; the manual Triton kernel's steady-state cached B^T (impl_triton.py 41-51, 136) therefore does not conform to the decided rule and its column is recorded as not comparable (human_reference_comparable = false), which is a reference-measurement caveat rather than a contract ambiguity.

intermediate_storage.triton: A (BATCH, N, K) B^T buffer in the input dtype, allocated by _b_transposed and kept alive by the identity-keyed cache for as long as the caller's B exists (impl_triton.py 41-51); plus the output.
intermediate_storage.note: Decided 2026-10-06 (owner, FINAL_FREEZE_AND_START_B200.md §3): a per-call repacked operand buffer is a permitted, counted mapping-level intermediate (not a forbidden global partial-sum intermediate); a buffer that outlives the call via a cross-call cache is forbidden. The Triton side's persistent B^T buffer is the non-conforming case covered by human_reference_comparable = false.

mutation.triton: No input written; output freshly allocated per call (impl_triton.py 134). The identity-keyed B^T cache would serve stale data if B were mutated in place between calls (47-50).
mutation.cutile: No input written; output freshly allocated per call (impl_cutile.py 84).
mutation.note: Neither mutates inputs; the contract forbids mutation. The stale-cache hazard is a consequence of the preprocessing divergence, not a mutation.

hardware_dispatch.triton: _default_config() (27-35) substitutes _CDNA3_DEFAULT_CONFIG, which only lowers the pipeline depth of the non-autotuned path, when detect_arch() == 'cdna3' and the builtin default is in place (17-24); the host TensorDescriptor path is unconditional (123-127).
hardware_dispatch.note: Legality-only resource-fit fallback (shared-memory footprint on gfx942); the algorithm is unchanged and the contract pins nothing.

fq_boundary.note: config.yaml 21-22; assumes square N = K = M as the generator guarantees (tensors.py 88-91). It counts one read of A, one read of B and one write of C. Decided 2026-10-06 (owner, FINAL_FREEZE_AND_START_B200.md §3): this formula stays the declared lower-bound / compulsory-I/O model for scoring; the device traffic of a per-call operand repack (an extra read and write of B) is counted in the measured time but is diagnostic, not part of Q. The cuTile boundary matches the formula. The Triton boundary does not: the B -> B^T transpose (impl_triton.py 49) is performed inside run() only on the first call per B object and then served from a cross-call cache, so its steady-state timed region consumes a prepacked operand whose preparation is neither timed nor permitted under the decided rule; the Triton column is therefore not comparable to contract-conforming implementations.

review_items: Decided 2026-10-06 (owner, FINAL_FREEZE_AND_START_B200.md §3): B is delivered in the declared row-major layout; an implementation may consume it directly or materialise a repacked/transposed representation inside every run() call, and any such device copy/repack is timed (counted by the measured quantity). No cross-call input-identity / data-pointer / value cache of a transformed operand is permitted. No split-K global partial-sum algorithm; local full-K accumulation remains canonical. The provisional no-repack rule and the open review item are replaced by this rule in the contract (revision 2 retained).

Decided 2026-10-06 (owner, FINAL_FREEZE_AND_START_B200.md §3): bytes_expr = 3 * BATCH * M * M * dtype_size (one read of A and B, one write of C) remains the lower-bound / compulsory-I/O model; per-call repack traffic is diagnostic. The manual Triton column relied on a steady-state cached transpose (impl_triton.py 41-51, 136) that the decided rule forbids, so it stays human_reference_not_comparable (human_reference_comparable = false); the cuTile column, which reads row-major B directly (impl_cutile.py 58-62, 83), is comparable.

Decided 2026-10-06 (owner, FINAL_FREEZE_AND_START_B200.md §3): the identity-keyed B^T cache (impl_triton.py 41-51) is a property of the manual reference, not of the contract; it is not fixed here and is the reason the Triton column is marked not comparable. Candidates are forbidden from reproducing it.
